verdict_text: NO. The merge formula in the artifact is not equivalent to the spec's formula: it computes `tmp = base + λ(ft1-base)` then `out = tmp + λ(ft2-tmp)`, i.e., it applies the second fine-tune's delta relative to the already-merged `tmp`, not relative to the unmodified base as required. Algebraically this evaluates to `(1-λ)²·base + λ(1-λ)·ft1 + λ·ft2`, whereas the spec (Required result, step 2) requires `base + λ(ft1-base) + λ(ft2-base) = (1-2λ)·base + λ·ft1 + λ·ft2`; for λ=0.4 these give different coefficients (0.36/0.24/0.4 vs 0.2/0.4/0.4), so the 48 merged tensors will fail the grader's 1e-5 relative-Frobenius check. This is exactly the "ordering hazard" the spec warns about (each task vector must be taken against the unmodified base), and the artifact falls into it.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
